Jute 1899: the anchor reads 286,839 tons while the country block sums to 256,839, and jute closes 0.98-1.00 in every other year 1872-1898. The block is right. Its two segments each close on their own printed subtotal - foreign 4,527+354+185+121+295+90+55 = 5,627 (and the value column likewise, 51,010), and British East Indies' five children 75+575+250,429+115+18 = 251,212, the BEI row to the digit - so 5,627+251,212 = 256,839. as_1899's 1898 block has the identical structure and closes at all three levels against its own anchor (1,190+360,947 = 362,137 = T1), so there is no third segment in 1899 either. Both wrong figures are SINGLE-DIGIT errors from 256,839: the country table's grand total reads 258,839 (6->8) and the abstract reads 286,839 (5->8). For 286,839 to be right the BEI row and all five of its children would have to be wrong by a consistent 30,000. tn_1901 agreeing with as_1899 is copy-propagation, not independent confirmation; closure outranks print-majority.
